title: Small representative families of finitely presented scalar local models on a pro-etale site
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ and bounded small site skeletons as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and $A=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $U$ in the bound put $R_U=p_U^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-sfb-integral-model-condensed-coefficients]. Let $T$ be any scheme in that bound, with its $\mathcal V$-small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Modules are sectionwise sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], or equivalently internal modules via [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For a finitely presented scalar $A$-module $P$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], its scalar-extension model on $U$ is $R_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$. A module has a finite constant local model if its module pullback on a pro-étale covering of $T$ is isomorphic on each member $U$ to such a scalar-extension model, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; pullback uses [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. There exist a set $I_T\in\mathcal V$ and modules $(F_{T,t})_{t\in I_T}$, each having a finite constant local model, such that every $R_T$-module having a finite constant local model is isomorphic to some $F_{T,t}$. The local scalar models may be indexed by $Q=\coprod_{m,n\in\mathbf N}\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(A)$, using the actual modules $P_q=A^n/\operatorname{im}(q:A^m\to A^n)$ and their scalar extensions; no local-model sheaves defined by arbitrary matrices of $R_U$-sections are required. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, torsion-freeness or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis is imposed on $T$.

proof.text: Finite presentations on the condensed point are coded by natural numbers n,m and a map between regular finite free modules. Each finite presented module is isomorphic to the cokernel of one of these maps, so these point models have a small label type.

Pullbacks along a pro-etale cover are jointly faithful on internal coefficient modules. The cartesian coefficient map is an isomorphism; extendScalarsIsoComapInv reduces equality to equality of underlying abelian inverse images. The proved localization comparison identifies these inverse images with restriction. Pull the original cover back along each test object and apply sheaf separatedness to prove equality. This includes the empty cover.

Repeat the proved prescribed-model counting argument directly for internal modules, using its private essentiallySmall_embeds helper. The witnessing covers have index type in Type u, so the type of all such covers of T lives in Type (u+1). Codes consist of one such cover and a point-model label on each member. For each code take the product of the actual lowerStar direct images of the models. Adjunction transposes local trivializations to a map from M to that product. The indexed cover and step 2 show this map is monic by cancellation through the local isomorphisms. Internal module categories are Grothendieck abelian, hence well powered. The small family of subobjects of each product and the small union over codes yield essential smallness. ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.exists_small_le chooses representatives that themselves satisfy the local condition.

Apply the continuous scalar finite-presentation comparison to each point module in a witnessing cover. An ordinary finite presented A-module is isomorphic to A^n/range(q) for a scalar matrix q: choose a finitely generated relation submodule and express its generators as a finite linear map. Transport the quotient equivalence through scalar realization and point pullback. Conversely every such quotient is finitely presented, since the range of its finite free source is finitely generated. The continuous scalar comparison gives a finite presented point module for each such model. These two arguments give the exact second conjunct on the same cover.
